precepts.text: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” David heard the Lord speak unto his Lord: the Father speaking, and the Son seated at his right hand. It is the same distinction David makes between the Lord my rock and the God of my rock.

David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. The Rock that begat Israel is Christ, and the God of that Rock is the Father who set him at his right hand.

precepts.text: David is not ascended into the heavens, but he himself says the Lord said unto my Lord, sit thou on my right hand; so let all the house of Israel know that God has made that same Jesus, whom they crucified, both Lord and Christ.
precepts.point: The Lord said unto my Lord, sit thou at my right hand until I make thine enemies thy footstool. The one sitting at the Father's right hand is Christ.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” Peter tells who is speaking and who is sitting: “For David is not ascended into the heavens: but he saith himself, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Until I make thy foes thy footstool.”

David is not the one at the right hand; he is not ascended into the heavens. He himself says the Lord said it unto his Lord. “Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ.”

The one sitting at the Father's right hand is Christ, that same Jesus whom they crucified, and all the house of Israel is to know it assuredly.

precepts.text: The beast, America, is slain and its body destroyed and given to the burning flame, its allies' lives prolonged for a season for slavery; then one like the Son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days and is given an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away.
precepts.point: Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning; thou hast the dew of thy youth. Israel is patiently waiting to be saved.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion: rule thou in the midst of thine enemies.” The rod is Christ ruling in the midst of the enemies, and Daniel shows how that rule comes.

“I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame. As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time.” The beast, America, is slain and its body destroyed and given to the burning flame; its allies' lives are prolonged for a season, for slavery.

Then “one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days”, and “there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.” That is the rod of his strength sent out of Zion, an everlasting dominion in the midst of his enemies. Israel is patiently waiting to be saved, willing in the day of his power.

precepts.text: Jesus shall be called the Son of the Highest, and the Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David; He shall reign over the house of Jacob forever and of His kingdom there shall be no end.
precepts.point: Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning; thou hast the dew of thy youth. Israel is patiently waiting to be saved.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David”.

The rod of strength sent out of Zion is Jesus, given the throne of his father David. “And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.” His people, the house of Jacob, shall be willing in the day of his power, and Israel is patiently waiting to be saved under that reign that has no end.

precepts.text: Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH, referring to Christ; He shall build the temple of the Lord, bear the glory, sit and rule upon His throne, and be a priest upon His throne.
precepts.point: The Lord hath sworn and will not repent, thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. Christ is the priest forever after this order.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.” Zechariah shows the same man, a king who is also a priest: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord”.

The BRANCH is Christ. “Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” He sits and rules upon his throne and is a priest upon that throne at the same time. That is the priest forever after the order of Melchizedek, sworn by the Lord who will not repent.

precepts.text: Christ shall rebuke the wicked inventions of the nations and destroy them without labor by the law, which is like fire.
precepts.point: He shall drink of the brook in the way, therefore shall He lift up the head. God is waiting on us, on Israel, to keep His laws so He can activate and do His thing.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“He shall judge among the heathen, he shall fill the places with the dead bodies; he shall wound the heads over many countries.” Ezra shows how: “this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest; And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame: and he shall destroy them without labour by the law which is like unto me.”

Christ is going to destroy the heathen, and it will be very light work, without labour, by the law, which is like fire. The Lord at the right hand, the commandments, strikes through kings in the day of his wrath.

precepts.text: Because of these words, the Lord makes His words in the mouth fire and this people wood, and it shall devour them; God's word and His law are like fire.
precepts.point: He shall drink of the brook in the way, therefore shall He lift up the head. God is waiting on us, on Israel, to keep His laws so He can activate and do His thing.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“Wherefore thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Because ye speak this word, behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.” God's word and his law are like fire, and the people are wood.

That is why the destroying of the heathen is without labour: the law that is like fire devours them. He fills the places with the dead bodies and wounds the heads over many countries by his word in the mouth.

precepts.text: Cursed be the deceiver; for the Most High is a great King and His name is dreadful among the heathen, because when Israel starts keeping God's laws the heathen know they are finished.
precepts.point: He shall drink of the brook in the way, therefore shall He lift up the head. God is waiting on us, on Israel, to keep His laws so He can activate and do His thing.

note.label: Psalm 110: Sit Thou at My Right Hand

precepts.why:
“But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.”

The Most High is a great King, and his name is dreadful among the heathen, because when Israel starts keeping God's laws the heathen know they are finished. “He shall drink of the brook in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head”: God is waiting on us, on Israel, to keep his laws so he can activate and do his thing, striking through kings and judging among the heathen.

precepts.text: Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
David wrote, “The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” This is written in the psalms concerning Christ, who after he suffered and rose sits at the right hand of the Father until his enemies are made his footstool.

It is another of the things Christ came to fulfil, a prophecy of himself, which shows again that fulfilling the law and the prophets is about what was written of him, not the ending of the commandments.

precepts.text: The psalm quoted: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
precepts.point: Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces, and the chief seats in the synagogues. What they wanted was the recognition of men.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
“How say the scribes that Christ is the Son of David? For David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool.” This is the psalm he quoted: “The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.”

David, by the Holy Ghost, calls Christ “my Lord”. “David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son?” The scribes called Christ the son of David and stopped there; David himself called him Lord, seated at the right hand of the Lord until his enemies are made his footstool. The common people heard him gladly. The scribes, who loved long clothing, salutations in the marketplaces and the chief seats in the synagogues, wanted the recognition of men, and they missed what David saw.

precepts.text: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
precepts.point: David himself did not ascend, but said the Most High told his Lord to sit at his right hand until his foes are made his footstool, another prophecy pointing to Christ.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Peter quotes David word for word: “The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.” David himself did not ascend into the heavens, so he is not speaking of himself. The Lord told David's Lord to sit at his right hand until his foes are made his footstool.

David's Lord is Christ, exalted by the right hand of the Most High. It is another prophecy pointing to Christ, and Peter uses it to show that the one raised up and seated at the right hand is the one David wrote about.
